name: Benaiah
overview: Benaiah was a male warrior from the tribe of Ephraim, known specifically as the Pirathonite. He held a distinguished position as the eighteenth member of "the thirty," a group of David's elite men. Additionally, he was entrusted with leadership over the eleventh division of Israel's military forces, reflecting his significant role in David's reign.
namesAndTitles: The name Benaiah means "YHWH has built," indicating a theologically rich meaning rooted in God's providence. This proper name highlights a connection to the Lord's sustaining power, as recorded in 2 Samuel 23:30.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Benaiah as an Ephraimite, linking him to the tribe of Ephraim as an ancestor. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Benaiah's importance in the biblical narrative stems from his status as one of David's elite warriors, known as "the thirty," and his leadership role over a military division. His position reflects both his valor and the trust placed in him by King David, marking him as a key figure in the consolidation of David's kingdom and military organization.
